CORE VERSION: the 12.4 line kept moving (12.4.5, 12.4.6, 12.4.7 on 2026-08-04, 12.4.8 on 2026-08-07) so the pin is now FOUR patches behind, but every one of those release bodies was read and NONE contains a security section or a CVE reference -- freshness, not exposure. No advisory affecting 12.4.x has been published since 12.4.4. TWO METHODOLOGY TRAPS FOUND HERE, both of which would have produced a false finding, and both worth carrying forward because they will recur every cycle: (1) OSV IS UNUSABLE FOR THIS PACKAGE. Querying api.osv.dev for github.com/grafana/grafana at version 12.4.4 returns THIRTY-NINE vulns, which reads like an alarm; inspecting the records shows the 2026 ones carry ranges of literally [{introduced: '0'}] with NO fixed event, so they match EVERY version ever released. An OSV version query for grafana is a false-positive generator, not a scan. Use GHSA (which carries real ranges -- e.g. CVE-2025-41117 is >=12.2.0,<12.2.5 and >=12.3.0,<12.3.3, i.e. below the 12.4 line) or grafana.com/security/security-advisories. Note also that GHSA's Go-module ranges for CVE-2026-33380/33381 are pseudo-versions ('< 1.9.2-0.20260513165311-fb7336fc36c1') describing grafana-as-a-LIBRARY, which do not map to the OSS distribution's 12.x at all. (2) A WEB-SEARCH SUMMARIZER INVENTED A CVE. It asserted, twice and confidently, that 'CVE-2026-13438' was fixed in 12.4.7 and 13.0.5. That id DOES NOT EXIST: cveawg.mitre.org returns CVE_RECORD_DNE, it appears in no release body, and it is absent from Grafana's own advisory index. It was NOT filed. The rule this vindicates: search results are a pointer to a primary source, never a finding. PROBE (docker_escape_paths) -> REM-197, and the shape of it is the lesson: the grafana role's compose template does not stop at Grafana -- its tail renders the exporter fleet, and cAdvisor in that fleet is the single highest-privilege container in the estate. privileged:true, uid 0, SecurityOpt label=disable, host / at /rootfs, /sys + /var/lib/docker + /var/run bound, on observability_net AND the flat shared_net. The docker socket is LIVE and it took work to prove because the surface lies twice: `ls -l` shows /var/run/docker.sock as a symlink to /Users/pazny/.docker/run/docker.sock (the /var/run:ro bind shadows the explicit socket bind and drags in the macOS host's own /var/run), which reads as dangling -- but /proc/self/mountinfo shows /host-services/docker.proxy.sock bound at exactly that path, and cat returns ENXIO (it IS a socket) not ENOENT. And `:ro` on a socket bind is cosmetic: it blocks unlinking the file, not the API, which is request/response over that socket. docker info confirms no rootless and no Enhanced Container Isolation. So code execution in cAdvisor is host root via POST /containers/create {Privileged:true, Binds:['/:/host']}. WHAT MAKES IT ACTIONABLE RATHER THAN THEORETICAL IS THE VALUE SIDE, MEASURED: Prometheus holds ONE series for container_cpu_usage_seconds_total and ONE for container_memory_usage_bytes, both id='/' -- ZERO per-container metrics, which is cAdvisor's entire purpose. /api/v1.3/docker returns 0 containers. The log is an infinite 'failed to identify the read-write layer ID ... /rootfs/var/lib/docker/image/overlayfs/layerdb/...: no such file or directory' loop, because /rootfs is macOS while the real /var/lib/docker is inside the LinuxKit VM. Maximum privilege, no delivered value. Rated exploitable-post-foothold not remotely-triggerable: :8080 answers 200 unauthenticated to any shared_net peer (same host-map-is-not-a-network-gate error as REM-194) but serves only read-only metrics and no secret, and cAdvisor has no published CVE. Fix: drop it on Darwin, or route it through the docker-socket-proxy the estate ALREADY runs for portainer and traefik and de-privilege it. v0.49.1 vs upstream head v0.60.5 is hygiene only -- the privilege is in our compose file, not their release notes.

portainer.notes: Cycle-35 batch-57 (2026-08-21, CVE scan + ssrf_vector_analysis). NOT CLEAN -- and the previous four batches that called it clean were not wrong, the world moved. CVE-2026-72533 / GHSA-jxhm-qq8x-v4c6 was published 2026-08-18, CVSS 4.0 9.4, and its range >=2.40.0 <2.45.0 covers the running 2.44.0. Filed REM-212 CRITICAL. Precondition is an authenticated NON-ADMIN, which this estate does produce: Authentik tier-1 gates who gets a session, but an OAuth-provisioned Portainer account is a standard user, not an administrator. MITIGATION MEASURED, not assumed: portainer runs --host tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375, and the LIVE proxy env has PLUGINS=0 (which independently neutralises the older CVE-2026-44848), ALLOW_START/STOP/RESTARTS=0, SECRETS=0, CONFIGS=0 -- but POST=1 and EXEC=1, so the bypass still reaches POST /containers/{id}/exec into any already-running container. Reduced from host RCE to broad in-container command execution; not closed. METHOD NOTE: OSV returned NINE portainer advisories for 2.44.0 and ALL NINE were false positives (Go introduced:0 range mapping; every one fixed at 2.33.8/2.39.2/2.41.0). The one real CRITICAL appears only on the vendor's GHSA endpoint. An OSV-only scan would have reported this component clean. RE-READ NEXT BATCH regardless of rotation -- an unpatched CRITICAL is what the 14-day drift window is too slow for. Prior probe REM-182 (CVE-2026-55761 uninitialised-instance takeover) remains correctly MITIGATED: the instance is initialised.

That is the evidentiary standard REM-144 explicitly could not meet (split-horizon dnsmasq had resolved its 'public' test back to the LAN, so it correctly refused to claim internet exposure); future probes should reach for --resolve against the authoritative public address before either claiming or disclaiming reach. It also overturns the 'pre-auth leg is CLOSED' disposition rustfs had carried since batch-36 -- the leg is not closed, it is narrowed to /health and /favicon.ico, and /health is the one that talks. THE GENERAL LESSON, which is about TIME rather than about headers: an advisory verdict is only true as of the hour it was read. REM-187 recorded rustfs's advisory leg clean at 04:12 and predicted, from this vendor's demonstrated habit of retroactively naming later releases as sole-patched, that beta.11 would likely acquire advisories anyway. Six were published at 14:13 the same day -- four against beta.11 and two against beta.12, the very version REM-187 recommended bumping TO. The prediction was right within ten hours, which means for a no-CVE prerelease vendor a clean verdict must carry its timestamp and a short shelf life. Pair that with the version disclosure above and the two findings compose: the estate publishes, anonymously and worldwide, exactly the string an attacker needs to know when this host's version enters an affected range. SECONDARY PATTERN, the probe's nominal quarry across all five: the components with NO HTTP surface are not automatically silent. MariaDB's pre-auth MySQL handshake advertises '11.8.8-MariaDB-ubu2404' -- application version AND Ubuntu base image -- to anyone who can open a socket, which is protocol-inherent and unfixable by config; Redis under --requirepass answers '-NOAUTH Authentication required.' to INFO, PING and LOLWUT alike and discloses nothing, a protocol-design difference rather than a configuration one. Neither is filed (both are loopback-bound with no router), but the sidecar observation is worth carrying: redis_exporter republishes redis_version="8.10.0" on an unauthenticated /metrics, so an exporter can undo the reticence its service carefully maintains. And qgis_server returns `Server: Apache/2.4.18 (Ubuntu)` -- one header fingerprinting a 2019 Ubuntu 16.04 userland -- which is not a new row but is the cleanest possible evidence for REM-184; it does not reach the internet only because REM-185's missing Authentik Provider makes the edge 404 first. --- PRIOR: Cycle-17 batch-38 FIRST RUN of this probe type, over woodpecker/jellyfin/traefik/uptime_kuma/calibreweb (2026-07-30): 4 items (REM-144 CRITICAL, REM-145 HIGH, REM-146 LOW, REM-147 LOW) + REM-148. Looking for leaked version strings surfaced leaked CREDENTIALS -- Traefik's dashboard/API answered anonymously at the edge because traefik_auth_modes.traefik='none', and /api/http/middlewares served rendered customRequestHeaders verbatim, disclosing X-Wing-Edge-Token, X-Face-Edge-Token and global_password_prefix itself. Lesson recorded there: 'oidc' means the edge is open and the app's own login is the only gate; 'none' means there is no gate at all. Also: security-headers@file strips NO response headers, it only adds, so any upstream Server or X-Powered-By passes through the edge untouched.

THE PROBE'S FINDING OF RECORD (REM-223): A VERSION NUMBER DOES NOT DESCRIBE THE ARTIFACT. tileserver-gl is at v5.6.0, which is the newest release that exists -- npm latest, zero advisories on the repo, the sole OSV entry fixed six years and two majors below the pin. Its version leg is permanently, correctly, unimprovably GREEN, and it will report green in every future cycle. Underneath it the container carries 56 pending Ubuntu -security updates including libc6, a libcurl four security revisions behind, and a ca-certificates trust store dated 20240203. There is no version to bump; the fix is an image rebuild nobody currently asks for. This is the previous run's lesson ('scanning versions answers is-the-number-old, never is-the-number-load-bearing') one turn further out: the number can be perfect and the artifact still stale, and no scanner in this estate looks inside (REM-225).

THE SECOND PATTERN, which is what makes the first actionable: IMAGE AGE DOES NOT PREDICT PACKAGE STALENESS -- BASE-DISTRO CHOICE DOES. Measured across all five, pending -security packages against image age: tileserver (Ubuntu 24.04, 140 days) 56; jellyfin (Debian 13 trixie, 79 days) 14; uptime-kuma (Debian 12 OLDSTABLE, 23 days) 11 but including Chromium three majors behind; traefik (Alpine 3.24, 24 days) 2, both apk-tools; woodpecker (scratch, 5 layers, no shell) 0 with no surface to accumulate on. The 23-day-old image is worse positioned than the 79-day-old one. So a freshness heuristic keyed on image age would have ranked these almost exactly backwards, and the useful question is not 'when was this built' but 'what is it built ON'.

Every figure above comes from a re-run with --user 0 where the package manager exited 0. RULE FOR THIS PROBE TYPE: assert the package manager's exit status before counting its output.
